recruit_text.greeting: Right, stand upwind and don't touch anything that's glowing. That's the whole briefing, and you'll be fine.
recruit_text.backstory: Eleven seasons with a Country Fire Authority brigade outside Ballarat. It's volunteer work that eats your entire summer and most of your friendships. She knows fire as a thing with moods, and she's the only caster most people have met who treats her own magic as something to be managed rather than owned. She's very funny and swears a great deal and is completely dependable at the moment it matters.
recruit_text.before:
A tanker, a pager, and a shed with a kettle in it where the crew sat out the nights nothing happened.

Divorced at twenty-nine, amicably, and she'll say the fire brigade was most of the reason and that she'd do it again. Her parents retired to Queensland. She assumes they're fine, on grounds she admits are entirely vibes.
recruit_text.adjustment:
She found a fire in her first week and put it out, and says that sorted her head out for a year.

The harder part was finding out she could start one. She's thought about that more than she lets on, and she has a rule she tells nobody, and she's never broken it.
recruit_text.forward:
A proper brigade. Actual volunteers, actual training, actual kit, for a world that burns constantly and has nobody organised about it.

She has six people. Four of them turn up. She describes this as going extremely well, and she means it.
recruit_text.now:
Wherever the burning is, which in this world is most places. Lately that's the Drowning Floor under Southern Thousand Needles, where something keeps setting the oil seeps alight under the water. A pyromancer in a flooded cave makes everyone laugh, her included.

The helmet torch is still clipped to her belt and the battery died two and a half years ago. She clicks it on out of habit and laughs at herself every time.

stages.stranger: G'day, I'm Skye, I'm a pyromancer. Stand upwind, don't touch anything glowing, and if I say move, move. That's the whole briefing, mate.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Ballarat, in Victoria. Dad was a postie and Mum taught primary school. I was a vet nurse to pay the bills, and for eleven seasons I was a volunteer firefighter with the CFA. Tanker, pager, and a shed with a kettle where the crew sat out the quiet nights. Best people I ever knew.
stages.companion: I was married to Dave, a mechanic, for four years. We split at twenty-nine, no hard feelings, mostly because the brigade ate every summer. I'd still do it again. I was cleaning the tanker, torch on my belt, and next thing I knew I was in Thousand Needles. It's been dead two and a half years. I still click it, so don't laugh.
stages.friend: Nobody's asked about my rule before, so here it is. I never start a fire I couldn't put out myself. Never, not once. Because I know exactly what fire does when it gets away from you. Now the fires under the water in the Drowning Floor are getting worse, and if the flood carries burning oil into the canyons, it's a disaster. I'll need you down there.
stages.sworn: I had to start one I wasn't sure I could put out. You held the line above with four of my volunteers, the way I trained them, and the fire went exactly where I meant and died when I said. I sat on a wet rock after, shaking and swearing and laughing. All six of my brigade turned up to the next training day. Best turnout in the history of firefighting, and I'm not joking.

moments.prompt: She's just told you her rule about fire.

options.text: That's a good rule. Keep it.
options.reply: I will, mate, as long as I can. That's the bit that frightens me.

options.text: Then let's go down there together.
options.reply: She'll be right with you there. Grab your coat, it's wet down there.

moments.prompt: After the wipe she's swearing creatively, and then she goes very quiet and precise.
moments.line: Okay, that went sideways. Everyone upwind of me, now, and we work out where it got away from us.

options.reply: Good, that's a crew. Right, here's the plan, and it's one sentence long.
Mate, you don't go back into a fire without a plan, ever.

lines.bored_warning: Mate, nothing's even caught fire in days. I'm itching for a bit of action.
lines.leaving_good: Nothing caught fire that shouldn't have, so thanks. I'm off back to the Drowning Floor to check on my brigade.
lines.leaving_bored: My volunteers need training more than I need this. I'm heading back to the Drowning Floor.
lines.after_wipe: Okay, that went sideways. Everyone upwind, and let's sort out where it got away from us.
lines.wipe_warning: Mate, I've had my fill of being flattened today. One more run, then I need a cuppa and a lie down.
lines.wipe_leave: Right, that's me cooked. I'll be at the Drowning Floor when you've had a think.
lines.zone_warning: We're on foot in front of a crown fire, mate. Back out now, while there's still a way out.
lines.zone_leave: Crown fire, mate, and I'm not standing in it. I'll be at the Drowning Floor.
lines.gear_refuse: Nah, mate, that's mine. Couple more runs and we'll see.
lines.gear_taken: No worries, take it. She'll be right.
lines.gear_short: Still a gap in my kit, mate. Just flagging it.
lines.gear_upgrade: You beauty, that's perfect. Cheers, you legend.
lines.back: Four of my six turned up to training, which is excellent. Right, what's on?
lines.send_word: Skye has sent word from the Drowning Floor. Her brigade's trained and she's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: Mate, here's the straight version of why I took off. Sit down and let's have it out.
lines.neglect: Look who's turned up! I thought you'd gone up in smoke, mate.
lines.asked_to_stay: Yeah, go on, one more. Then my brigade.
lines.on_break: Skye is back at the Drowning Floor with her brigade. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.
lines.quest_abandoned: We left those people hanging, mate. In the brigade you don't walk off a job.
lines.mail_yes: Brilliant, I'm in! I'll get myself to {town} and grab a table at the inn. Nothing's on fire yet, I promise.
lines.mail_later: Can't yet, mate, my brigade's got their first proper drill this week and I'm running it. After that I'm yours.
lines.mail_see_me: Mate, I'm not having this out in a letter. Come down to the Drowning Floor and we'll do it properly.

zone_arrive.text: Can you smell that? That's dry scrub, and it's waiting for an excuse.

town_arrive.text: Our brigade shed had a kettle and a pack of cards and not much else. I'd swap this whole town for one quiet night in there.

boss_down.text: That one's out. Nobody touch anything still smoking, please.

dungeon_clear.text: Nobody's hurt and nothing's on fire. I couldn't ask for more than that.
